CITY OF LA VERNE

  PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  MEETING AGENDA

  Wednesday, June 9, 2021, 9:00 a.m.
  Watch Live at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream
  3660 D Street, La Verne, CA 91750

The Public Financing Authority meeting for La Verne’s Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District will
be closed to the public in compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the
spread of the COVID-19 Virus. However, the public is encouraged to participate in this meeting in
any of the following ways:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream
  2) Please submit your written comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org. They will be
  shared with the Authority Members prior to the meeting and will be made part of the
  permanent record. We ask that you provide those emails before 7:00 p.m. the day before the
  meeting. Please be advised that public comments submitted by emails or any other
  format to the City are public records that will be made available for public viewing.
  3) Participate on Zoom by registering here before 8:00 am the day of the meeting:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_5bFRpWrdSK6rgGd4rB1ERg
  4) For individuals that wish to share their comments during the live stream, you may email
  planning@cityoflaverne.org by 8:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting with a phone number and
  the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the appropriate time during the
  meeting for your comment.

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Assistant City
Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.
_________________________________________________________________________________

 2. Aooroval of Minutes - March 3,2021
3. lnfrastructure and Facility Reimbursement Aoreement - At their March 10,2021 meeting,
  the Public Financing Authority Board heard proposed financing options in order to implement
  the initial projects listed in the lnfrastructure Financing Plan. Based on direction and input by
  the City Council, the Board directed staff to prepare an agreement that would have the City
  provide the initial funds with a repayment component. At their May 17,2021 meeting, the City
  Council approved the draft lnfrastructure and Facility Reimbursement Agreement, pending
  approval by the Board.

  Staff recommends that the Authority Board approve PFA Resolution No. 21-02 approving
  the lnfrastructure and Facility Reimbursement Agreement.

4. Annual Reoort - Per State Law, the Public Financing Authority is required to adopt an annual
  report of activities undertaken within the last fiscal year. This is the first annual report of the
  District, and was mailed out to all property owners and participating taxing entities (County).

  Staff recommends that the Authority Board approve PFA Resolution No. 21-03, adopting
  the submitted Annual Report for fiscal year 2020-2021.

5. PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS - This is the time set aside for anyone
  wishing to address the Public Financing Authority on items not listed in any other place on the
  agenda. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the legislative body is prohibited from talking or
  engaging in discussion on any item not appearing on the posted agenda. However, your
  concerns may be referred to staff or set for discussion at a later date. The Chair reserves the
  right to place limits on duration of comments.

6. ADJOURNMENT - The next regularly scheduled meeting of the Public Financing Authority will
  be held on Wednesday, September 8, 2021, and is expected to be held virtually at
  www. citvoflaverne. orq/stream

  Posting Statement: On June 3,2021, a true and correct copy of this Agenda was posted on the
  bulletin board at La Verne City Hall, La Verne Police Department, and on the City's website

   LA VERNE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District (EIFD)
  Minutes of a Special Meeting
  Wednesday, March 3, 2021
  Teleconference
  ___________________________________________

1.  The Public Financing Authority meeting for La Verne’s Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District
  was closed to the public in compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the
  spread of the COVID-19 Virus. Additionally, the meeting was conducted via teleconference with
  all Authority members and members of the public participating remotely.

2.  A Special meeting of the La Verne Public Financing Authority was called to order by Vice- Chair
  Carder at 9:02 a.m.

3.  Board Members Present: Mayor Tim Hepburn, Vice-Chair Robin Carder, and Raymond Skelton,
  Gilbert Ivey, and Anish Saraiya representing Los Angeles County Supervisor Barger.

  Board Member Absent: Chair Los Angeles County Supervisor Barger.

  Staff Present: Executive Director Robert Russi, Community Development Director Eric Scherer,
  and Deputy City Attorney Peter Wallin.

4.  La Verne Public Financing  It was moved by Hepburn, seconded by Ivey, and carried by a
  Authority Enhanced  vote of 4-0 (Barger absent) to approve the La Verne Public
  Infrastructure Financing District  Financing Authority Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District
  (EIFD) Minutes  (EIFD) Minutes of August 12, 2020.

5.  Amendments of Bylaws  Community Development Director Scherer reported on the
  proposed Public Finance Authority (PFA) amendments to the
  Agency’s Bylaws. He stated that as a result of the reformation
  of the Public Financing Authority (PFA) Board, it is necessary to
  amend the bylaws which were adopted in 2017. He reported
  that the makeup of the Board has changed to include a member
  of the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors. Amending
  the bylaws will allow for the appointment of Supervisor Kathryn
  Barger to the PFA Board and allow her to assign an alternate to
  fill her seat and vote when she is unable to attend meetings.

  Community Development Director Scherer reported on other
  proposed minor modifications to be consistent with the bylaws
  adopted by other County PFAs, as follows:

   Defining the role of the Board
   Defining the duties of the Executive Director
   Changing the timing of the election of officers
   Changing the regular meeting dates from monthly to
  quarterly
   Providing more details on how the bylaws can be amended
   Adding a certification that these are the approved bylaws.

  Community Development Director Scherer introduced and
  welcomed Anish Saraiya representing the Office of Los Angeles
  County Supervisor Barger. Mr. Saraiya will be attending future
  meetings representing Supervisor Barger on the Board.
 Public Financing Authority Minutes (EIFD), Wednesday, March 3, 2021, page 2

  It was moved by Ivey, seconded by Hepburn, and approved by
  roll call with a vote of 4-0 (Barger Absent) to approve the
  amendments to the bylaws as proposed.

  6.  Update on Financing Options  Executive Director Russi reported on Financing Options to
  begin to plan for the implementation of the Infrastructure
  Financing Plan along with a power point presentation.
  Executive Director Russi also explained how the District would
  serve as a financing mechanism for agencies to fund or issue
  bonds for an array of public projects as well as support
  economic development efforts in special areas. He stated that
  the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District funds would be
  used to facilitate development adjacent to the future Gold Line
  Station and complete the public improvements of the Old Town
  La Verne Specific Plan.

  The Board Members discussed the different financing options
  noting that it would be a long-time before the District can
  generate funds for the proposed projects and that it would be
  beneficial to market the area now for developer interest.
  The Board Members expressed support for having the City fund
  the priority projects, namely the Pedestrian Bridge and
  Streetscape Improvements for pedestrian movement pursuant
  to an agreement by which the District would reimburse the City.
  The City would look at other sources, like grant money, Edison
  Rule 20a, before using City funds.

 7.  Public Comment  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS - This is
  the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the
  La Verne Financing Authority on items not listed in any other
  place on the agenda. Under the provisions of the Brown
  Act, the legislative body is prohibited from talking or
  engaging in discussion on any item not appearing on the
  posted agenda. However, your concerns may be referred to
  staff or set for discussion at a later date. Any person desiring
  to speak were asked to email their comments prior to the close
  of the public comment period including their name and address
  for the record. The Chair reserves the right to place limits on
  duration of comments.

  Vice Chair Carder called for public comment and waited a few
  minutes for staff to check for any public comments received via
  email. There was none.

  8.  Meeting was adjourned at 9:44 a.m., and adjourned to Wednesday, June 9, 2021 at 9:00 a.m.

  Respectfully submitted,

  Lupe Gaeta Estrella, CMC
  Secretary/Assistant City Clerk

 INFRASTRUCTURE AND FACILITY REIMBURSEMENT AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF LA VERNE AND
THE LA VERNE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY

THIS INFRASTRUCTURE AND FACILITY REIMBURSEMENT AGREEMENT (“Agreement”) is entered into as
of June _________, 2021, by and between the LA VERNE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY, a local public
agency formed pursuant to Chapter 2.99 (commencing with Section 53398.50) of Part 1 of Division 2 of
Title 5 of the Government Code (“PFA”), and the CITY OF LA VERNE, a municipal corporation (“City”).

RECITALS

  A. The PFA has adopted an Amended and Restated Enhanced Infrastructure Financing Plan (“Plan”)
  for the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District No. 1.

  B. The PFA and the City desire to enter into this Agreement to provide interim financing for certain
  of the projects included in the Plan (“Priority Projects”) by allowing the City to advance funds to
  finance those projects and to be reimbursed from future tax increment monies, bond proceeds
  or any other funds lawfully available to the PFA. The Priority Projects are described on Exhibit A
  attached hereto.

  C. In instances where the City has included the Improvements in its budget or Capital
  Improvements Program, the City has done so with the expectation that the PFA will pay for or
  reimburse the City for its payment of the cost thereof. No moneys of the City were, are, or are
  reasonably expected to be available on a long‐term basis for design, installation and
  construction costs of the Priority Projects.

NOW, THEREFORE, the parties hereby agree as follows:

Section 1. Purpose of this Cooperation Agreement. The City and the PFA acknowledge the above recitals
and desire to enter into this Cooperation Agreement to provide for the advance by the City and the
payment or reimbursement by the PFA of the costs of the design, installation and construction of the
Priority Projects. Pursuant to this Cooperation Agreement, the PFA agrees to pay to or for the benefit of
the City the cost of design, installation and construction of the Priority Projects, including payment of
related costs, subject to the provisions of this Cooperation Agreement. In order to timely undertake the
Priority Projects, the City will either advance the cost of the Priority Projects to the PFA or shall
undertake the Priority Projects improvements directly. The PFA shall pay for, or reimburse to the City,
not more than the cost advanced to the PFA by the City or paid by the City to design, install and
construct the Priority Projects, which costs are approximated in Exhibit A. Prior to the City undertaking
any of the projects the PFA shall first deliver to the City the PFA' s finding and determination that the
PFA has, or will have, sufficient moneys to pay for or reimburse the City on a lump ‐sum basis or by
periodic payments over a period of years for all of the cost of the design installation and construction of
the Priority Projects then being undertaken by the City. Following receipt of such finding and
 determination, the City shall proceed to undertake the subject project subject to appropriation of funds
by the City Council for such purpose.

Section 2. Construction and Installation. The City shall perform all required preparatory work for the
Priority Projects, including compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act and shall install and
construct, or cause to be installed and constructed, the Priority Projects. The City shall retain a person or
entity experienced in the design and construction of the Improvements to undertake the design of the
Improvements and to prepare plans and specifications therefore. The City shall, in accordance with all
applicable federal, state and local laws, rules and regulations, install and construct, or cause to be
installed and constructed, the Improvements in accordance with such plans and specifications.
Alternatively, upon notice thereof and direction from the City, the PFA shall perform such preparatory
work, installation and construction.

Section 3. Reimbursement Costs. The City shall, following completion of each Priority Project, or
various portions thereof, submit to the PFA quarterly statements showing the cost of the improvements
incurred by the City due to be paid by the PFA pursuant to this Cooperation Agreement. Such amounts
may include progress payments.

Section 4. Reimbursement by the PFA. Within a reasonable time after the submission of each quarterly
statement to the PFA pursuant to Section 3 hereof, the PFA shall pay to or for the benefit of the City all
amounts due thereunder. The parties recognize that repayment may occur over a period of time.
Amounts not paid by the PFA to the City within 30 days of demand therefore shall bear interest at the
then current rate of the Local Agency Investment Fund (“LAIF Rate”).

Section 5. Obligation to Pay Subordinate to Other Obligations. The obligation of the PFA to make
payment to the City shall, without necessity of further action by the PFA or City, be junior and
subordinate to all other obligations or indebtedness heretofore or hereafter voluntarily incurred by the
PFA.

Section 6. Nonliability of Officials and Employees. No PFA Board member, Councilmember, or Treasurer,
and no official, agent, or employee of the PFA or the City shall be personally liable to the other parties,
or any successor in interest, in the event of any default or breach by the PFA or the City, or for any
amount which may become due to the City or PFA, or successor, or on any obligations under the terms
of this Cooperation Agreement.

Section 7. Future Cooperation. The parties hereto agree to take all appropriate steps and execute any
documents which may reasonably be necessary or convenient to implement the intent of this
Cooperation Agreement.

Section 8. Records. Each party shall maintain books and records regarding its duties pursuant to this
Cooperation Agreement. Such books and records shall be available for inspection by the officers and
agents of the other party and by the public at all reasonable times.
 Section 9. Law Governing. This Cooperation Agreement is made in the State of California under the
constitution and laws of the State of California, and is to be so construed.

Section 10. Amendments. This Cooperation Agreement may be amended at any time, and from time to
time, by an agreement executed by both parties to this Cooperation Agreement.

Section 11. Severability. Whenever possible, each provision of this Cooperation Agreement shall be
interpreted in such a manner as to be valid under applicable law. If any provision of this Cooperation
Agreement is determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, void or unenforceable, the
remaining provisions shall nevertheless continue in full force and effect.

Section 12. Implementation Memoranda. From time to time, the City Manager and the Executive
Director of the PFA may execute implementation memoranda, to evidence, in addition to this
Cooperation Agreement, the indebtedness of the PFA to the City created by this Cooperation Agreement
and the program and/or plan for implementing any of the provisions hereof.

Section 13. Liability and Indemnification. Pursuant to Section 895. 4 of the Government Code, the PFA
and the City agree that each will assume the full liability imposed on it or any of its officers, agents or
employees for injury caused by a negligent or wrongful act or omission occurring in the performance of
this Cooperation Agreement, and each parry agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the other party for
any loss, cost or expense that may be imposed on the other parry by virtue of Section 895. 2 and 895. 6
of the Government Code.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Agreement to be executed the day and year first
above written.

Dated this________________________ of June, 2021

CITY OF LA VERNE
City Manager’s Office
DATE:  May 17, 2021

TO:  Honorable Mayor and City Council

FROM:  Bob Russi, City Manager

SUBJECT:  Resolution 21-24 - Approval of Infrastructure and Facility Reimbursement
  Agreement with the Public Financing Authority for La Verne’s Enhanced
  Infrastructure Financing District
______________________________________________________________________
AGENDA SUMMARY

At the City Council’s February 16, 2021 Study Session, staff presented funding alternatives for initial
projects outlined in the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District’s (District) Infrastructure Financing
Plan (IFP). The Council provided direction to discuss the alternatives with the Public Financing
Authority (PFA) with a recommendation that the City provide the initial funding with a reimbursement
agreement with the PFA. The PFA met on March 10, 2021, and agreed with the approach, directing
Staff to prepare such an agreement.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council approve Resolution 21-24, approving the draft Infrastructure
and Facility Reimbursement Agreement which outlines the priority projects between the City and the
PFA, with the PFA scheduled to review and approve the agreement at their June 9, 2021 meeting.

BACKGROUND

In 2017, the City first established the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District (District), creating
the Public Financing Authority (PFA) who subsequently approved the Infrastructure Financing Plan
(IFP) which outlined 14 specific projects at an anticipated cost of $33 million. In 2019 and 2020, the
District, PFA and, IFP were amended and reinstated with the County of Los Angeles agreeing to
participate in the District.

Now that the District is established, Staff has examined alternatives in procuring the funding to begin
the first round of projects listed in the IFP. The nature of the District relies on the property tax
increment to generate the monies to pay for the projects. By design, upon the initial creation, these
monies are significantly lower than what is necessary to fully fund the projects outlined in the IFP. By
our estimates, it will take approximately 10 years from the formation of the District to generate the
revenue to be able to support a bond to pay for the priority projects.

The alternative funding mechanisms, including simply waiting until the District has generated enough
revenue, were presented to the City Council and the PFA earlier this year. Both bodies agreed that
the best path forward would be for the City to facilitate the construction of the initial priority projects
utilizing a variety of potential resources (grants, Prop. C funds, CIP dollars, etc.) with the PFA
agreeing to reimburse the City, with 1% interest, at a later date. The draft agreement provides for this
to occur and identifies the priority projects that are expected to be funded.
